title: The Fallen Hero and Rakh’likh
summary: Two faction paths lead to Trebor, whose return to the Blasted Lands is bound to his captured soldiers. Their spirits are freed, and the search for a demon’s true name and a Felbane weapon leads to Razelikh.
opening: An old soldier’s defeat has not ended his duty. Across separate Alliance and Horde introductions, the trail reaches Trebor and the soldiers still held by the powers of the Blasted Lands.

chapters.title: Two Roads and the Old Wound
chapters.body:
The Blasted Lands lay exposed beneath old ruin, and Trebor’s defeat still burdened those he had commanded. Different appeals brought the living to his spirit: a hope of common resistance to the Legion, or the search for orders lost in an ambush. They met at an old soldier whose concern had outlasted his life. He could not forget the men he had failed to save.

In the Swamp of Sorrows, Bengor lay wounded after an ambush. The dispatch had been struck, and the Warchief’s orders were lost. His report led the seeker toward Trebor. Before the fallen soldier’s shame could be understood, the missing command had to be recovered. Through the wet and shadowed country, an urgent duty opened the way toward an older defeat.

Trebor remembered a failed battle and his return to the Blasted Lands to rescue the men left behind. He had been unable to abandon them to torment. Even the number of those lost remained uncertain, but the obligation endured. Death had not released their commander from the knowledge that his soldiers still suffered beneath the power that had overcome them.

Razelikh and his lieutenants—Sevine, Allistarj and Grol—held Trebor’s soldiers in bondage. Stones maintained the hold upon their tortured souls. Across the exposed red earth, the seeker worked to break those bindings. The old defeat was no longer only a memory. Something of its cruelty could still be answered, and those denied rest might yet be released.

chapters.title: Release and the Amulet
chapters.body:
With the binding stones broken, the tortured souls could rest. Trebor had received the mercy he had sought for his soldiers. Their names and losses could not be restored to the living, but the torment that followed them had eased. Beyond that release remained the power behind their captivity. The demon’s servants had lost their hold; their master still stood.

At Serpent’s Coil, Kirith the Damned barred the way. The open badlands narrowed toward a cave upon the coast. There the adventurer defeated the demon, and Kirith’s spirit offered knowledge the living had not possessed. The encounter brought the search nearer its hidden purpose, yielding a clue to the power that had held Trebor’s soldiers.

Kirith’s spirit revealed that Razelikh could not be reached until a shattered amulet was made whole. Its three pieces were held by the demon’s lieutenants. The scattered fragments gave the search a shape. To answer Trebor’s grievance, the seeker would need the means to approach the master himself, and more than courage to endure the meeting.

chapters.title: A Name and a Weapon
chapters.body:
On Azshara’s cold eastern shore, Loramus Thalipedes offered counsel. The demon hunter directed the seeker toward Razelikh’s true name and a weapon with which to challenge him. Wind-cut coast and pale ruins replaced the Blasted Lands’ dry scar. The old soldier’s burden had led far from its beginning, into a search for knowledge that could make the final confrontation possible.

Among Azshara’s pale coastal ruins, the seeker gathered Hetaera’s blood and sought Lord Arkkoroc’s knowledge. Beneath the title Razelikh the Defiler lay a truer name: Rakh’likh. Old temple stone and blue water framed the discovery. The enemy who had seemed distant behind his servants’ bindings could now be named, though the means to defeat him had yet to be prepared.

A name alone could not break the Defiler’s hold. Azsharite was gathered in Azshara for the making of Felbane weaponry. The search had found its target; now the material for the confrontation passed into the seeker’s hands. Beside the old coastal ruins, preparation followed knowledge, carrying Trebor’s appeal nearer the power it was meant to challenge.

At Galvan’s camp in inland Stranglethorn, the gathered material became Felbane weaponry. Green canopy and hanging vines sheltered the work, far from Azshara’s cold shore. What had been carried through the search could now serve in battle. The prepared armament joined the true name, while the broken amulet still awaited the recovery of its scattered pieces.

With the weapon prepared, the seeker returned toward Trebor and the exposed Blasted Lands. There the old captivity and the new preparations converged. The demon’s name was known, and Felbane weaponry could be brought against him. Yet the way to the Rise remained closed until the amulet’s fragments were reunited. The last burden still lay with his lieutenants.

chapters.title: The Defiler Unbound
chapters.body:
Allistarj, Sevine and Grol each held a piece of the amulet. Separate confrontations yielded the fragments. When they were brought together, the broken object became whole again. The way Kirith had described could now be opened. Trebor’s plea had gathered knowledge, a weapon and the means of approach; the master behind the bindings remained to be faced.

At the Rise of the Defiler, the united amulet brought the demon within reach. Razelikh was Rakh’likh, the enemy whose true name the seeker had learned. Those who gathered against him carried the purpose begun among Trebor’s bound soldiers. At last, every preparation met its end in a confrontation with the master whose servants had denied them rest.

Razelikh was defeated. His horn was carried back to Trebor as a sign of hope, together with the Ward of the Defiler, which the old soldier intended to destroy. The bound souls had found release, and the demon who held them had fallen. Across the Blasted Lands, one long obligation had reached its answer, though the Legion’s greater shadow remained.

reviewNote: Complete 15-scene illustrated research story with linked source/citation/claim/event records, distinct faction openings, a separate Horde courier scene, Classic area-specific art, principal cast and pivotal objects. 15 transcript-matched AI narration tracks are generated (436 seconds total) and still require human listening and pronunciation review. Quest and dialogue details are currently traced through secondary Classic database reproductions; capture the original 1.12-era client/build before human lore approval. The eighteen-stone/nineteen-soldier conflict stays unresolved; the lieutenant scenes are independent encounters; Loramus’s later Cataclysm retelling is excluded; the ward is returned for Trebor to destroy but its destruction is not asserted as shown; and Razelikh’s defeat is not the defeat of the Burning Legion. The art is original and interpretive; compare each place and character to the matching Classic build before approval.
